screenSummary.playArea: A star-filled planetarium view from the observer's location shows the Sun, Mercury, the horizon, and their angular separation.
screenSummary.controlArea: Observer location sets where on Earth the sky is seen from. View controls choose what the camera follows, zoom, and whether the atmosphere and cardinal points are drawn. Time controls set the date, step by solar or sidereal days, animate time at several rates, or jump between greatest elongations.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Drag the sky or choose a view mode, then change the date or play time to compare each body's motion against the stars.

screenSummary.playArea: A top-down ecliptic view shows the Sun, Mercury, Earth, their orbit paths, and the elongation measured at Earth. An events readout names the last and next conjunction or greatest elongation.
screenSummary.controlArea: Time controls set local mean solar time, step by solar or sidereal days, animate time at several rates, or jump between greatest elongations. A checkbox shows or hides the elongation angle.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Change the date or play time to connect the orbital geometry with Mercury's observed elongation.
